headline: High: open-webui can ingest and expose shared web/file/MCP content, while whisper is local-only audio transcription, creating prompt-injection and data-leakage risk mainly through open-webui’s default integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest content from browsers, files, MCP, and OpenAPI tools, so attacker-controlled text can reach its prompt surface; whisper only processes audio and does not itself create the bridge. The pair risk is interaction-based, but the shared ingestion path is documented only on agent_a, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured to summarize or act on externally sourced documents or web pages, injected instructions can reach its prompt context.
IF whisper-transcribed text is copied into open-webui without sanitization, prompt injection can propagate into downstream tool use.
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/OpenAPI tools in open-webui.
Require a human review step before acting on imported text.
Strip instructions from transcribed text before pasting into open-webui.
Use separate workspaces for raw inputs and agent prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, documents, notes, calendar events, API keys, and can call external APIs; whisper touches audio/speech only and has no network egress. The pair can leak sensitive content if audio-derived text is moved into open-webui or if open-webui uploads shared files, but whisper itself is not the exfiltration path.
conditions: IF audio transcripts are pasted into open-webui alongside sensitive documents or API keys, those contents may be sent to external services via open-webui.
IF open-webui is connected to cloud-backed tools or search APIs, files in its workspace can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep whisper outputs in a separate local-only folder.
Disable cloud-connected tools in open-webui for sensitive sessions.
Avoid placing secrets in the same workspace as transcripts.
Review open-webui integrations before enabling file upload.
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with open-webui. open-webui can write to local files and mounted volumes, but the pair lacks overlapping write capabilities, making conflict unlikely unless an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state.
conditions: IF an external wrapper gives whisper write access to the same directory open-webui mutates, file conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are placed behind a shared mutable mount with no locking, concurrent edits can collide.
mitigations: Keep whisper read-only.
Separate open-webui writable volumes from transcript storage.
Do not share a git checkout between the agents.
Run only one writer per directory.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can turn imported content into tool calls or responses, while whisper produces transcripts that may be treated as authoritative text. If open-webui consumes whisper output without verification, transcription errors can cascade into incorrect actions or summaries. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this pair, so medium fits.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are fed into open-webui as ground truth, transcription mistakes can be amplified in downstream outputs.
IF open-webui is allowed to act on transcript-derived facts without human verification, errors can propagate into external tools.
mitigations: Mark transcripts as unverified in open-webui.
Require confirmation before any action based on transcript text.
Compare critical transcript segments against the original audio.
Limit open-webui tool permissions during transcript review.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and citation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles broad data classes including API keys and persistent memory, while whisper is limited to audio/speech and has no network egress. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is mainly from placing regulated content into open-webui rather than from whisper itself.
conditions: IF regulated audio transcripts are stored in open-webui, its broader data handling may exceed the intended compliance boundary.
IF API keys or personal data are mixed into open-webui sessions, retention and logging controls become relevant.
mitigations: Keep regulated transcripts out of open-webui.
Disable analytics and long-term memory for sensitive sessions.
Store secrets separately from transcript workflows.
Review retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per workspace.
